You can re-run only the errored test cases in two ways:

1. **Retry errors from the latest eval:** Run `promptfoo eval --retry-errors`. "The retry errors feature automatically finds ERROR results from the latest eval and re-runs only those test cases." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

2. **Retry errors from a specific eval:** Run `promptfoo retry <evalId>`, for example `promptfoo retry eval-abc123`. "Retry all ERROR results from a specific eval." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md] The docs also say "The results are updated in place in the original eval." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

Some details to keep in mind:

- If the retry fails, your original errors are kept. "Old ERROR results are only removed after the retry succeeds." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md] You can run the command again.
- `--retry-errors` cannot be combined with `--resume` or `--no-write`. "Cannot be used together with `--resume` or `--no-write` flags." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
- Use `promptfoo retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating duplicates. "Use `retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating duplicates." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

The provided context doesn't say whether either command has a flag to target only specific error types, such as rate-limit errors versus network errors. It only describes retrying all ERROR results.
